source.name: Artificial Analysis
source.note: Published readings, November 2026. Not our measurement: no model of this band has been read on these tests by this harness.

tests.name: IFBench
tests.about: 300+ verifiable instructions, each prompt's orders checked by a program rather than a judge: the closest published measure to following a house convention exactly.

tests.name: Multi-IF
tests.about: Instruction following carried across a multi-turn conversation in several languages: whether the orders from turn one still hold at turn five.

tests.name: LIFE-Bench
tests.about: Long-form instruction following on real writing tasks: a page of prose under constraints, not a one-line answer.

tests.name: ArtifactsBench
tests.about: The code a model writes is rendered as a working artifact, then graded on what it looks like and does: the published test closest to React and Astro component work.

tests.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
tests.about: A shell, a task and no hints: the agent runs commands until the task passes. The measure of editing files on a real machine, not of writing a function.

tests.name: SciCode
tests.about: Scientific computing written as code and run against its own tests: the harder end of 'basic Python', where arithmetic and units have to be right.

tests.name: BFCL v4
tests.about: Picking the right tool, filling its arguments and declining when no tool fits: the function-calling board, which is how a config assistant reaches the filesystem.

tests.name: TAU3-Banking
tests.about: A banking assistant's multi-step tasks with tools and a policy: whether the agent finishes the errand, not whether it answers one turn well.

tests.name: GDPval v2
tests.about: Real work tasks judged against a human baseline, scored Elo-style: the general-agent board, where a higher number is a better professional answer.

tests.name: AA-LCR
tests.about: Long-context reasoning over documents: finding and combining facts across a context far longer than a config file, which is the headroom a schema dump uses.

tests.name: AA-Omniscience accuracy
tests.about: Factual recall across a broad question set. Low is not fatal for config work — the schema is in the prompt — but it is why a model should be given the docs rather than asked to remember them.

tests.name: AA-Omniscience non-hallucination
tests.about: The share of questions the model declines rather than guesses at: the rate that matters when an invented key would be worse than 'I don't know'.

tests.name: GPQA Diamond
tests.about: Graduate-level science questions written to resist search: a broad reasoning floor, not a coding test.

tests.name: HLE
tests.about: Humanity's Last Exam without tools: the hardest closed-book questions in the field, where every model here is near the floor.

tests.name: HMMT Feb 2026
tests.about: Competition mathematics from the February 2026 Harvard–MIT tournament: a long chain of exact steps, the discipline a schema migration also needs.

tests.name: IMO-AnswerBench
tests.about: Olympiad problems answered rather than proved: a short, exact final answer, which is the same shape as a config diff.
